newsitem.title: USA: Shut Santa Fe pipeline forces truck delivery.
newsitem.headline: Shut Santa Fe pipeline forces truck delivery.

text.p: The shutdown of the Sante Fe Pacific Pipeline from San Francisco to Reno, Nevada, is forcing Bay area refiners to consider shipping petroleum products by truck, a state official said Tuesday.
"They are having to make other arrangements, like trucking," said Alexia Retallack of the California Office of Oil Spill Prevention and Response.
An apparent leak was discovered over the weekend in a section of line in California's Sierra Nevada mountains.
On Tuesday, crews were digging through thick snow to find the source of the leak.

The eight-inch segment of pipeline, operated by Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline Partner LP, carries jet fuel, diesel, and gasoline to Reno. The state official did not know how much product was being shipped at the time of apparent leak.
One trader for Bay area refiner said his company might truck up supplies if any Reno customers were short of supply.
Spot prices for products were relatively flat on Tuesday, traders said.
